counterexample: Initial selected config: format0, root_format2, ultimate_profiles_count0, one game-mode row with nonzero binding B and a Configurator communication backend; healthy accepted v2 phase2 store. B held at boot, not MB1. Validator does not require format1 when root_format2.

Normal setup skips count>0 migration and skips final root!=2 compact save. Default Configurator primary installed; boot binding B is marked consumed. Configurator has no scan, so boot B state remains.

Successful legacy SET1 retains format0 and uses game_mode_configs_count0, backend default_mode0; no embedded profiles required. Next Normal loop has no matching row and resets mode_chord_consumed=false.

Successful legacy SET2 uses one game row plus a valid legacy schema-v1 profile with nested tables/Coords and nonzero scalar. _config format0 permits it; its root_format is rewritten0. Mode masks are not rebuilt by FinalizeSetConfig, so original nonzero B mask remains.

Next Normal loop sees row0 and original B mask, calls destination_selector with backendConfigurator. persist_mode_destination executes LoadConfigChecked before rejecting Configurator. It decodes selected D4 current before returning Refused.
The backend/descriptor route is Configurator CDC; no NES constructor existed in this epoch. Use Config348, not mode408. This does not refute the successfully migrated format1 case.
